short_description: Brosolve contains bromfenac, a non-steroidal anti-inflammatory eye medicine used around cataract surgery.
full_description: Brosolve contains bromfenac, a non-steroidal anti-inflammatory eye medicine used around cataract surgery. It reduces prostaglandin activity associated with ocular pain and inflammation. Treatment is limited to the surgeon’s prescribed schedule because prolonged or inappropriate use may delay healing or cause serious corneal adverse effects.
dosage_guidance:
Dosing and Schedule
For the 0.09% twice-daily formulation used as the reference: instil 1 drop into the operated eye twice daily for 14 days, starting the day after cataract surgery. The source strength of 0.00% must be corrected and the twice-daily formulation confirmed before publication.

Administration Advice
Wash hands and place the prescribed drop inside the lower eyelid without touching the dropper tip. Close the eye gently. Separate other eye medicines by at least 5 minutes.

benefits.title: Pain Associated with Cataract Surgery
benefits.description: Helps reduce ocular pain during the prescribed perioperative or postoperative treatment period.

benefits.title: Inflammation Associated with Cataract Surgery
benefits.description: Helps control postoperative inflammation when selected by the ophthalmologist.

mechanisms.title: 01 — Acts within Ocular Tissues
mechanisms.description: Bromfenac penetrates ocular tissues after topical application.

mechanisms.title: 02 — Inhibits Cyclo-Oxygenase
mechanisms.description: The active medicine reduces cyclo-oxygenase-dependent prostaglandin synthesis.

mechanisms.title: 03 — Reduces Pain and Inflammation
mechanisms.description: Lower prostaglandin activity helps control surgery-related ocular symptoms.

safety_sections.title: NSAID Allergy and Bleeding
safety_sections.description: Avoid if previous aspirin or NSAID use caused asthma, swelling or allergy. Inform the doctor about anticoagulants and bleeding disorders.

safety_sections.title: Corneal Damage and Delayed Healing
safety_sections.description: Diabetes, dry eye, corneal disease and prolonged treatment increase risk. Seek urgent review for pain, reduced vision or worsening redness.

safety_sections.title: Contact Lenses and Other Eye Medicines
safety_sections.description: Remove contact lenses and follow the surgeon’s advice on reinsertion. Use with steroid eye drops only under supervision.

composition_summary: Astaxanthin 4 mg Zeaxanthin 4 mg + Lutein 20 mg + Vit A 2500 IU Vit C 240 mg + Vitamin E Acetate 120 IU Softgel Capsules
short_description: Optivro combines lutein, zeaxanthin and astaxanthin with vitamins A, C and E for ocular nutritional support.
full_description: Optivro combines lutein, zeaxanthin and astaxanthin with vitamins A, C and E for ocular nutritional support. These nutrients participate in retinal or antioxidant functions. It may complement dietary measures when appropriate, but this formulation should not be presented as an AREDS2-equivalent supplement or a treatment that restores lost vision.
dosage_guidance:
Dosing and Schedule
Adults: take 1 softgel capsule once daily.

Administration Advice
Take with or immediately after a meal. Review continued use with the treating clinician and avoid overlapping supplements.

benefits.title: Inadequate Ocular Micronutrient Intake
benefits.description: Supplies selected carotenoids and vitamins when dietary intake is insufficient and the clinician considers this combination appropriate.

benefits.title: Adjunct Retinal Nutritional Support
benefits.description: May complement an individual eye-care plan. The formula has not been established as a substitute for evidence-based AREDS2 treatment in eligible patients.

mechanisms.title: 01 — Supplies Retinal Carotenoids
mechanisms.description: Lutein and zeaxanthin are constituents of macular pigment.

mechanisms.title: 02 — Provides Antioxidant Nutrients
mechanisms.description: Vitamins C and E and the carotenoids participate in antioxidant processes.

mechanisms.title: 03 — Supports Normal Visual Nutrition
mechanisms.description: Vitamin A contributes to visual-cycle function when intake is adequate. Supplementation does not reverse established retinal damage.

safety_sections.title: Vitamin A and Pregnancy
safety_sections.description: Check the vitamin A form and total intake. Excess preformed vitamin A can harm a fetus.

safety_sections.title: Duplicate Antioxidants and Interactions
safety_sections.description: Review other vitamins, anticoagulants and cancer treatment before use. Avoid assuming more antioxidant supplementation is better.

safety_sections.title: Eye Disease Assessment
safety_sections.description: New distortion, sudden vision loss or a visual-field change requires urgent examination. Supplements do not replace retinal treatment.

composition_summary: Brinzolamide 1% w/v Eye Drops
short_description: Brinstar contains brinzolamide, a prescription eye medicine that lowers raised intraocular pressure.
full_description: Brinstar contains brinzolamide, a prescription eye medicine that lowers raised intraocular pressure. It reduces aqueous humour production by inhibiting carbonic anhydrase in the eye. It is used in appropriate open-angle glaucoma or ocular hypertension, with regular checks to assess pressure control and tolerability.
dosage_guidance:
Dosing and Schedule
Adults: instil 1 drop into each affected eye three times daily, at evenly spaced intervals.

Administration Advice
Wash hands and place the prescribed drop inside the lower eyelid without touching the dropper tip. Close the eye gently. Separate other eye medicines by at least 5 minutes. Close the eyelids and press the inner corner for 1–2 minutes to reduce systemic absorption. Remove contact lenses as directed by the label. Shake the suspension well before use.

benefits.title: Open-Angle Glaucoma
benefits.description: Lowers raised eye pressure as part of prescribed treatment to reduce the risk of further optic nerve damage.

benefits.title: Ocular Hypertension
benefits.description: Helps control raised eye pressure when treatment is needed before detectable glaucomatous damage develops.

mechanisms.title: 01 — Inhibits Carbonic Anhydrase
mechanisms.description: Brinzolamide inhibits carbonic anhydrase II within the ciliary processes.

mechanisms.title: 02 — Reduces Bicarbonate-Dependent Secretion
mechanisms.description: Reduced bicarbonate formation decreases sodium and fluid transport into the eye.

mechanisms.title: 03 — Lowers Eye Pressure
mechanisms.description: Reduced aqueous humour production lowers intraocular pressure.

safety_sections.title: Sulfonamide Reactions and Kidney Disease
safety_sections.description: Carbonic anhydrase inhibitors may cause sulfonamide-type hypersensitivity. Severe kidney impairment or acid-base disturbance requires avoidance or specialist review.

safety_sections.title: Corneal Disease and Other Medicines
safety_sections.description: Corneal endothelial disease needs assessment. Review oral carbonic anhydrase inhibitors and high-dose salicylates.

safety_sections.title: Vision and Contact Lenses
safety_sections.description: Temporary blurring may occur. Follow preservative-related contact-lens advice and wait until vision clears before driving.

composition_summary: Gatifloxacin 0.3% w/v + ketorolac 0.4% w/v eye drops
short_description: Gatiquin-KT combines gatifloxacin with ketorolac for selected eye conditions requiring antibacterial treatment and non-steroidal control of pain or inflammation.
full_description: Gatiquin-KT combines gatifloxacin with ketorolac for selected eye conditions requiring antibacterial treatment and non-steroidal control of pain or inflammation. The antibiotic acts against susceptible bacteria, while ketorolac reduces prostaglandin formation. Use should follow ophthalmic assessment because the combination is unsuitable for every red or painful eye.
dosage_guidance:
Dosing and Schedule
This medicine is for external use only. Take it in the dose and duration as advised by your doctor.

Administration Advice
Wash hands and place the prescribed drop inside the lower eyelid without touching the dropper tip. Close the eye gently. Separate other eye medicines by at least 5 minutes.

benefits.title: Selected Bacterial Ocular Infection with Inflammation
benefits.description: May be prescribed when a susceptible bacterial infection and a separate need for an anti-inflammatory are both present.

benefits.title: Selected Perioperative Ocular Care
benefits.description: May be used when an ophthalmologist selects this combination for a defined surgical care plan under the local label.

mechanisms.title: 01 — Inhibits Bacterial DNA Enzymes
mechanisms.description: Gatifloxacin inhibits DNA gyrase and topoisomerase IV in susceptible bacteria.

mechanisms.title: 02 — Reduces Prostaglandin Formation
mechanisms.description: Ketorolac inhibits cyclo-oxygenase enzymes involved in ocular pain and inflammation.

mechanisms.title: 03 — Controls Two Distinct Components
mechanisms.description: The combination addresses bacterial infection and associated inflammatory symptoms when both treatments are appropriate.

safety_sections.title: NSAID Allergy and Bleeding
safety_sections.description: Avoid if previous aspirin or NSAID use caused asthma, swelling or allergy. Inform the doctor about anticoagulants and bleeding disorders.

safety_sections.title: Corneal Damage and Delayed Healing
safety_sections.description: Diabetes, dry eye, corneal disease and prolonged treatment increase risk. Seek urgent review for pain, reduced vision or worsening redness.

safety_sections.title: Contact Lenses and Other Eye Medicines
safety_sections.description: Remove contact lenses and follow the surgeon’s advice on reinsertion. Use with steroid eye drops only under supervision.

safety_sections.title: Antibiotic Allergy and Resistance
safety_sections.description: Avoid with relevant quinolone allergy. Do not use for viral or allergic conjunctivitis, and avoid unnecessary prolonged antibiotic exposure.

composition_summary: Brimonidine Tartrate 0.2% w/v Eye Drops
short_description: Brimway contains brimonidine, a prescription eye medicine that lowers raised intraocular pressure.
full_description: Brimway contains brimonidine, a prescription eye medicine that lowers raised intraocular pressure. It reduces aqueous humour production and increases its drainage through alpha-2 receptor activity. It is used in appropriate open-angle glaucoma or ocular hypertension, with regular checks to assess pressure control and tolerability.
dosage_guidance:
Dosing and Schedule
Adults: instil 1 drop into each affected eye three times daily, approximately 8 hours apart. Do not use in children younger than 2 years.

Administration Advice
Wash hands and place the prescribed drop inside the lower eyelid without touching the dropper tip. Close the eye gently. Separate other eye medicines by at least 5 minutes. Close the eyelids and press the inner corner for 1–2 minutes to reduce systemic absorption. Remove contact lenses as directed by the label.

benefits.title: Open-Angle Glaucoma
benefits.description: Lowers raised eye pressure as part of prescribed treatment to reduce the risk of further optic nerve damage.

benefits.title: Ocular Hypertension
benefits.description: Helps control raised eye pressure when treatment is needed before detectable glaucomatous damage develops.

mechanisms.title: 01 — Activates Alpha-2 Receptors
mechanisms.description: Brimonidine stimulates alpha-2 adrenergic receptors in ocular tissues.

mechanisms.title: 02 — Changes Fluid Dynamics
mechanisms.description: It reduces aqueous secretion and increases uveoscleral outflow.

mechanisms.title: 03 — Lowers Eye Pressure
mechanisms.description: Reduced fluid accumulation helps control intraocular pressure.

safety_sections.title: Infants, Children and Sedation
safety_sections.description: Brimonidine is contraindicated under 2 years and can cause serious sedation or breathing suppression in young children. Paediatric use requires specialist care.

safety_sections.title: Blood Pressure and Interactions
safety_sections.description: Review low blood pressure, cardiovascular disease, sedatives and monoamine oxidase inhibitors. Drowsiness and dizziness may occur.

safety_sections.title: Allergy and Follow-Up
safety_sections.description: Delayed allergic conjunctivitis can occur. Report persistent redness or swelling and attend regular pressure checks.

composition_summary: Flurbiprofen 0.03% w/v + hypromellose (HPMC) 0.25% w/v eye drops
short_description: Rixtear-F combines flurbiprofen with hypromellose for selected ophthalmic use around surgery.
full_description: Rixtear-F combines flurbiprofen with hypromellose for selected ophthalmic use around surgery. Flurbiprofen reduces prostaglandin formation, while hypromellose supports surface lubrication. The formulation may be used within an ophthalmologist-directed surgical plan, with the timing and purpose determined by the product’s approved directions rather than general dry-eye dosing.
dosage_guidance:
Dosing and Schedule
For prevention of intraoperative miosis in adults: instil 1 drop into the surgical eye every 30 minutes, beginning 2 hours before surgery, for 4 doses in total. Administration is directed by the surgical team.

Administration Advice
Wash hands and place the prescribed drop inside the lower eyelid without touching the dropper tip. Close the eye gently. Separate other eye medicines by at least 5 minutes.

benefits.title: Inhibition of Intraoperative Miosis
benefits.description: Flurbiprofen may be used before eye surgery to reduce prostaglandin-mediated pupil constriction.

benefits.title: Selected Perioperative Ocular Inflammation
benefits.description: May be used for an additional anti-inflammatory purpose only if supported by the exact local combination label and surgeon’s prescription.

mechanisms.title: 01 — Inhibits Cyclo-Oxygenase
mechanisms.description: Flurbiprofen reduces prostaglandin synthesis in ocular tissues.

mechanisms.title: 02 — Limits Prostaglandin-Mediated Responses
mechanisms.description: Reduced prostaglandin activity helps limit surgically induced pupil constriction and inflammatory responses.

mechanisms.title: 03 — Supports Surface Lubrication
mechanisms.description: Hypromellose provides a lubricating film but does not replace the surgical anti-inflammatory action.

safety_sections.title: NSAID Allergy and Bleeding
safety_sections.description: Avoid if previous aspirin or NSAID use caused asthma, swelling or allergy. Inform the doctor about anticoagulants and bleeding disorders.

safety_sections.title: Corneal Damage and Delayed Healing
safety_sections.description: Diabetes, dry eye, corneal disease and prolonged treatment increase risk. Seek urgent review for pain, reduced vision or worsening redness.

safety_sections.title: Contact Lenses and Other Eye Medicines
safety_sections.description: Remove contact lenses and follow the surgeon’s advice on reinsertion. Use with steroid eye drops only under supervision.

composition_summary: Brinzolamide 1%w/v + Timolol 0.5%w/v Eye Drops
short_description: Brinstar-TM combines brinzolamide with timolol to lower raised pressure inside the eye.
full_description: Brinstar-TM combines brinzolamide with timolol to lower raised pressure inside the eye. The ingredients reduce aqueous humour production through different pathways, and their combined effect can improve pressure control. It is prescribed for appropriate glaucoma or ocular hypertension when combination treatment is needed, with regular ophthalmic monitoring.
dosage_guidance:
Dosing and Schedule
Adults: instil 1 drop into each affected eye twice daily, approximately 12 hours apart. Continue regularly and reassess intraocular pressure at scheduled visits.

Administration Advice
Wash hands and place the prescribed drop inside the lower eyelid without touching the dropper tip. Close the eye gently. Separate other eye medicines by at least 5 minutes. Close the eyelids and press the inner corner for 1–2 minutes to reduce systemic absorption. Remove contact lenses as directed by the label. Shake well before use.

benefits.title: Open-Angle Glaucoma
benefits.description: Lowers raised eye pressure as part of prescribed treatment to reduce the risk of further optic nerve damage.

benefits.title: Ocular Hypertension
benefits.description: Helps control raised eye pressure when treatment is needed before detectable glaucomatous damage develops.

mechanisms.title: 01 — Reduces Aqueous Production
mechanisms.description: Brinzolamide inhibits carbonic anhydrase in the ciliary body.

mechanisms.title: 02 — Adds Beta-Blockade
mechanisms.description: Timolol blocks beta-adrenergic receptors and further reduces aqueous humour formation.

mechanisms.title: 03 — Lowers Intraocular Pressure
mechanisms.description: Reduced fluid production helps control pressure and reduce further optic nerve injury risk.

safety_sections.title: Asthma and Heart Conditions
safety_sections.description: Timolol-containing drops are contraindicated in asthma, significant bradycardia, certain heart blocks and uncontrolled cardiac failure. Eye drops can have systemic effects.

safety_sections.title: Interactions and Low Blood Glucose
safety_sections.description: Review oral beta-blockers, verapamil, diltiazem and other cardiac medicines. Beta-blockade may mask warning signs of hypoglycaemia.

safety_sections.title: Sulfonamide Reactions and Kidney Disease
safety_sections.description: Carbonic anhydrase inhibitors may cause sulfonamide-type hypersensitivity. Severe kidney impairment or acid-base disturbance requires avoidance or specialist review.

safety_sections.title: Application and Follow-Up
safety_sections.description: Use punctal pressure after instillation to reduce systemic absorption. Attend eye-pressure checks and seek advice for breathing difficulty, faintness or a slow pulse.

composition_summary: Moxifloxacin 0.5%w/v + Dexamethasone 0.1%w/v Eye Drops
short_description: Moxable-DM combines moxifloxacin with dexamethasone for selected eye conditions requiring both antibacterial treatment and corticosteroid control of inflammation.
full_description: Moxable-DM combines moxifloxacin with dexamethasone for selected eye conditions requiring both antibacterial treatment and corticosteroid control of inflammation. The antibiotic acts against susceptible bacteria, while the steroid reduces inflammation. An ophthalmologist should confirm the diagnosis because steroids can worsen certain infections and require eye-pressure monitoring.
dosage_guidance:
Dosing and Schedule
Instil 1 drop into each affected eye four times daily for 7 days, then reassess before continuing or tapering the steroid component.

Administration Advice
Wash hands and place the prescribed drop inside the lower eyelid without touching the dropper tip. Close the eye gently. Separate other eye medicines by at least 5 minutes. Shake if the pack identifies the product as a suspension.

benefits.title: Steroid-Responsive Ocular Inflammation with Bacterial Infection
benefits.description: May be prescribed when a superficial susceptible bacterial infection coexists with an inflammatory condition requiring a corticosteroid.

benefits.title: Selected Postoperative Inflammation with Bacterial Risk
benefits.description: May be used after eye surgery when the surgeon considers both ingredients necessary under the product’s approved directions.

mechanisms.title: 01 — Provides Antibacterial Activity
mechanisms.description: Moxifloxacin inhibits bacterial DNA gyrase and topoisomerase IV.

mechanisms.title: 02 — Suppresses Ocular Inflammation
mechanisms.description: Dexamethasone activates glucocorticoid receptors and reduces inflammatory mediator activity.

mechanisms.title: 03 — Addresses Two Treatment Needs
mechanisms.description: Antibacterial and anti-inflammatory actions work together only when both are justified by the diagnosis.

safety_sections.title: Eye Infection
safety_sections.description: Avoid in untreated fungal, viral or mycobacterial eye disease. Steroids can mask infection and worsen herpes-related corneal disease.

safety_sections.title: Eye Pressure and Healing
safety_sections.description: Prolonged use can raise eye pressure, cause cataract and delay healing. Monitoring is needed, particularly if treatment reaches 10 days.

safety_sections.title: Worsening Symptoms and Contact Lenses
safety_sections.description: Seek prompt review for increasing pain, light sensitivity or reduced vision. Avoid contact lenses during active inflammation or infection.

safety_sections.title: Allergy and Review
safety_sections.description: Avoid with relevant antibiotic allergy. Re-examine promptly if symptoms worsen or do not improve within 48 hours.

composition_summary: Natamycin 5% Eye Drops
short_description: Natvue contains natamycin, a topical antifungal suspension used for susceptible fungal infections of the eye, including fungal keratitis.
full_description: Natvue contains natamycin, a topical antifungal suspension used for susceptible fungal infections of the eye, including fungal keratitis. It acts on fungal cell membranes and requires frequent dosing in active corneal infection. An ophthalmologist should direct treatment and monitor response because delayed or inadequate therapy can threaten vision.
dosage_guidance:
Dosing and Schedule
Fungal keratitis: instil 1 drop into the affected eye every 1–2 hours initially. After 3–4 days of improvement, reduce to 1 drop six to eight times daily. Continue for 14–21 days or until the ophthalmologist confirms resolution; severe disease requires close review.

Administration Advice
Wash hands and place the prescribed drop inside the lower eyelid without touching the dropper tip. Close the eye gently. Separate other eye medicines by at least 5 minutes. Shake the suspension well before every dose. Follow storage and discard instructions precisely.

benefits.title: Fungal Keratitis
benefits.description: Treats susceptible fungal corneal infection, including appropriate Fusarium infections, under urgent specialist care.

benefits.title: Fungal Conjunctivitis or Blepharitis
benefits.description: May be prescribed for susceptible fungal infection involving the conjunctiva or eyelids.

mechanisms.title: 01 — Binds Fungal Membrane Sterols
mechanisms.description: Natamycin interacts with ergosterol in susceptible fungal membranes.

mechanisms.title: 02 — Disrupts Membrane Function
mechanisms.description: This impairs essential membrane transport and related fungal cell functions.

mechanisms.title: 03 — Controls Susceptible Fungal Infection
mechanisms.description: Local antifungal exposure limits infection when the organism is susceptible and treatment is maintained.

safety_sections.title: Urgent Corneal Monitoring
safety_sections.description: Increasing pain, light sensitivity, corneal opacity or reduced vision needs urgent review. Do not delay specialist treatment.

safety_sections.title: Steroids and Susceptibility
safety_sections.description: Do not add steroid drops without corneal-specialist advice. Resistant organisms or poor response require culture-based reassessment.

safety_sections.title: Allergy and Contact Lenses
safety_sections.description: Stop for a significant allergic reaction. Do not wear contact lenses during active ocular infection.

composition_summary: Tropicamide 0.8% w/v + phenylephrine hydrochloride 5% w/v eye drops
short_description: Ikarix combines tropicamide with phenylephrine to dilate the pupil for selected eye examinations or procedures.
full_description: Ikarix combines tropicamide with phenylephrine to dilate the pupil for selected eye examinations or procedures. Tropicamide reduces muscarinic activity in the iris and ciliary muscle, while phenylephrine stimulates the iris dilator. It is intended for professional ophthalmic use, with monitoring for ocular and cardiovascular adverse effects.
dosage_guidance:
Dosing and Schedule
Adults undergoing diagnostic pupil dilation: a healthcare professional instils 1 drop into the examination eye; repeat once after 5–10 minutes only if dilation is inadequate. Paediatric use requires a separate specialist regimen because this product contains phenylephrine 5%.

Administration Advice
For administration under professional direction. Apply punctal pressure for 1–2 minutes after the drop. Arrange help with travel if vision remains blurred or light-sensitive.

benefits.title: Diagnostic Pupil Dilation
benefits.description: Facilitates examination of the lens, vitreous and retina when the clinician considers dilation safe.

benefits.title: Pupil Dilation Before Selected Procedures
benefits.description: May be used to obtain mydriasis before an ophthalmic procedure according to the exact product label.

mechanisms.title: 01 — Blocks Muscarinic Receptors
mechanisms.description: Tropicamide relaxes the iris sphincter and reduces ciliary muscle accommodation.

mechanisms.title: 02 — Stimulates Iris Dilator Muscle
mechanisms.description: Phenylephrine activates alpha-1 adrenergic receptors and contracts the iris dilator.

mechanisms.title: 03 — Produces Mydriasis
mechanisms.description: The combined actions enlarge the pupil for the required examination or procedure.

safety_sections.title: Narrow Angles and Glaucoma
safety_sections.description: Dilation can trigger acute angle closure in susceptible eyes. Severe eye pain, headache or halos after use needs urgent assessment.

safety_sections.title: Cardiovascular and Endocrine Risks
safety_sections.description: Phenylephrine can raise blood pressure or disturb heart rhythm. Review heart disease, hyperthyroidism and interacting medicines.

safety_sections.title: Children and Temporary Visual Effects
safety_sections.description: Children may be more sensitive to systemic effects. Do not drive until vision clears and use protection from bright light.

composition_summary: Prednisolone acetate 1% w/v ophthalmic suspension (common reference salt and form assumed)
short_description: Predtos contains prednisolone, a corticosteroid eye medicine used for selected steroid-responsive inflammation.
full_description: Predtos contains prednisolone, a corticosteroid eye medicine used for selected steroid-responsive inflammation. It reduces inflammatory mediator activity and helps control redness, swelling and discomfort. Treatment requires an eye examination and an individual schedule because steroids can increase eye pressure, delay healing or worsen an unrecognised infection.
dosage_guidance:
Dosing and Schedule
Instil 1–2 drops into each affected eye two to four times daily. Use the examination-based frequency and taper written in the prescription. Reassess if there is no improvement within 2 days.

Administration Advice
Wash hands and place the prescribed drop inside the lower eyelid without touching the dropper tip. Close the eye gently. Separate other eye medicines by at least 5 minutes. Shake well before each dose once suspension identity is confirmed.

benefits.title: Steroid-Responsive Anterior Eye Inflammation
benefits.description: May be prescribed for selected conjunctival, corneal or anterior segment inflammation after infection has been evaluated.

benefits.title: Postoperative Ocular Inflammation
benefits.description: May help control inflammation after eye surgery when prescribed and monitored by the surgeon.

mechanisms.title: 01 — Activates Glucocorticoid Receptors
mechanisms.description: The corticosteroid binds intracellular glucocorticoid receptors in responsive ocular tissues.

mechanisms.title: 02 — Reduces Inflammatory Mediators
mechanisms.description: It alters gene activity and reduces inflammatory-cell recruitment and mediator production.

mechanisms.title: 03 — Controls Ocular Inflammation
mechanisms.description: Reduced inflammation can improve the prescribed steroid-responsive symptoms while monitoring continues.

safety_sections.title: Eye Infection
safety_sections.description: Avoid in untreated fungal, viral or mycobacterial eye disease. Steroids can mask infection and worsen herpes-related corneal disease.

safety_sections.title: Eye Pressure and Healing
safety_sections.description: Prolonged use can raise eye pressure, cause cataract and delay healing. Monitoring is needed, particularly if treatment reaches 10 days.

safety_sections.title: Worsening Symptoms and Contact Lenses
safety_sections.description: Seek prompt review for increasing pain, light sensitivity or reduced vision. Avoid contact lenses during active inflammation or infection.

composition_summary: Ketorolac (0.4% w/v) + Olopatadine (0.1% w/v) Eye Drop
short_description: Olgerix-KT combines olopatadine with ketorolac for selected allergic eye symptoms requiring an antihistamine and a non-steroidal anti-inflammatory.
full_description: Olgerix-KT combines olopatadine with ketorolac for selected allergic eye symptoms requiring an antihistamine and a non-steroidal anti-inflammatory. Olopatadine reduces histamine effects and mast-cell activation, while ketorolac limits prostaglandin formation. Use should be brief and ophthalmologist-directed because anti-inflammatory eye drops carry additional corneal and healing risks.
dosage_guidance:
Dosing and Schedule
Adults: instil 1 drop into each affected eye twice daily for allergy-related itching and inflammation. Reassess persistent symptoms before continuing the NSAID-containing combination.

Administration Advice
Wash hands and place the prescribed drop inside the lower eyelid without touching the dropper tip. Close the eye gently. Separate other eye medicines by at least 5 minutes.

benefits.title: Allergic Conjunctivitis with Itching
benefits.description: May be prescribed when allergic itching is accompanied by symptoms for which the clinician considers additional anti-inflammatory treatment appropriate.

benefits.title: Selected Inflammatory Allergic Eye Discomfort
benefits.description: May help selected allergy-associated discomfort after infection and other causes of a painful red eye are excluded.

mechanisms.title: 01 — Blocks Histamine and Mast-Cell Responses
mechanisms.description: Olopatadine reduces H1 receptor activation and allergic mediator release.

mechanisms.title: 02 — Reduces Prostaglandin Synthesis
mechanisms.description: Ketorolac inhibits cyclo-oxygenase enzymes involved in inflammatory pain.

mechanisms.title: 03 — Controls Selected Allergic Inflammation
mechanisms.description: The combined effects may relieve itching and associated inflammatory discomfort when both ingredients are indicated.

safety_sections.title: NSAID Allergy and Bleeding
safety_sections.description: Avoid if previous aspirin or NSAID use caused asthma, swelling or allergy. Inform the doctor about anticoagulants and bleeding disorders.

safety_sections.title: Corneal Damage and Delayed Healing
safety_sections.description: Diabetes, dry eye, corneal disease and prolonged treatment increase risk. Seek urgent review for pain, reduced vision or worsening redness.

safety_sections.title: Contact Lenses and Other Eye Medicines
safety_sections.description: Remove contact lenses and follow the surgeon’s advice on reinsertion. Use with steroid eye drops only under supervision.

composition_summary: Voriconazole 30 mg
short_description: Vorcore contains voriconazole for specialist treatment of selected fungal eye infections.
full_description: Vorcore contains voriconazole for specialist treatment of selected fungal eye infections. It interferes with fungal sterol synthesis and may be used for susceptible organisms in carefully monitored corneal infection. The final concentration depends on correct reconstitution, and treatment frequency, storage and duration must follow the actual ophthalmic product label.
dosage_guidance:
Dosing and Schedule
For a confirmed 1% solution: instil 1 drop into the affected eye every hour initially under corneal-specialist supervision. Reduce frequency only after documented improvement. The final reconstituted concentration must be verified before use.

Administration Advice
Reconstitute aseptically with the specified sterile diluent. A 30 mg vial yields 1% only at a final volume of 3 mL. Use the exact labelled final volume, storage and discard instructions. Keep the dropper tip sterile and separate other eye drops by at least 5 minutes.

benefits.title: Selected Susceptible Fungal Keratitis
benefits.description: May be prescribed by a corneal specialist after considering the likely or cultured organism and evidence-based first-line options.

benefits.title: Persistent or Resistant Fungal Corneal Infection
benefits.description: May be considered as a specialist alternative or adjunct when susceptibility and clinical response support use.

mechanisms.title: 01 — Inhibits Fungal Demethylase
mechanisms.description: Voriconazole inhibits fungal CYP51-dependent lanosterol demethylation.

mechanisms.title: 02 — Reduces Ergosterol Formation
mechanisms.description: Sterol depletion disrupts fungal membrane structure and function.

mechanisms.title: 03 — Limits Susceptible Fungal Growth
mechanisms.description: Local exposure can control susceptible fungi, with outcome dependent on organism and corneal penetration.

safety_sections.title: Vision-Threatening Infection
safety_sections.description: Fungal keratitis requires urgent follow-up. Worsening pain, opacity or vision needs immediate specialist review.

safety_sections.title: Concentration and Sterility
safety_sections.description: Incorrect dilution or contamination can seriously harm the eye. Do not prepare from a non-ophthalmic product without a validated sterile compounding process.

safety_sections.title: Steroids and Evidence
safety_sections.description: Avoid unsupervised steroid drops. Choice of voriconazole rather than natamycin should reflect organism-specific evidence and susceptibility.

composition_summary: Carboxymethylcellulose 0.3% w/w + glycerine 1% w/w + benzyl alcohol 0.1% w/w; listed as eye ointment
short_description: Fixtear Eye Ointment is listed as an ophthalmic lubricant containing carboxymethylcellulose and glycerine.
full_description: Fixtear Eye Ointment is listed as an ophthalmic lubricant containing carboxymethylcellulose and glycerine. These ingredients help retain moisture and reduce friction at the surface. The dosage form must be confirmed because an eye ointment, gel and solution require different administration instructions, and the supplied composition does not resolve that distinction.
dosage_guidance:
Dosing and Schedule
This medicine is for external use only. Take it in the dose and duration as advised by your doctor.

Administration Advice
Confirm whether the product is an ointment, gel or solution before administration. Wash hands, keep the applicator sterile and use after other eye drops when a true ointment is prescribed.

benefits.title: Dry Ocular Surface Discomfort
benefits.description: May provide lubrication for dryness-related irritation once the ophthalmic dosage form is verified.

benefits.title: Extended Lubrication When Clinically Appropriate
benefits.description: A verified viscous eye formulation may be selected for longer surface contact, including at bedtime when advised.

mechanisms.title: 01 — Provides Water-Binding Ingredients
mechanisms.description: Carboxymethylcellulose and glycerine retain water at the ocular surface.

mechanisms.title: 02 — Reduces Surface Friction
mechanisms.description: A compatible ophthalmic vehicle supports lubrication during blinking.

mechanisms.title: 03 — Improves Temporary Comfort
mechanisms.description: Improved hydration may reduce dryness-related irritation; residence time depends on the actual vehicle.

safety_sections.title: Persistent Pain or Vision Change
safety_sections.description: Stop and seek examination for eye pain, reduced vision, marked redness or symptoms that persist or worsen.

safety_sections.title: Dropper Hygiene and Discard Period
safety_sections.description: Do not touch the tip, share the bottle or use cloudy or discoloured solution. Follow the exact after-opening discard period.

safety_sections.title: Contact Lenses and Blurring
safety_sections.description: Check compatibility with contact lenses and remove them if the label requires it. Wait until temporary blurring clears before driving.

composition_summary: Brinzolamide 10 mg/mL (1% w/v) + brimonidine 2 mg/mL (0.2% w/v) + timolol 5 mg/mL (0.5% w/v) eye drops
short_description: Brinstar-BT combines brinzolamide, brimonidine and timolol for selected patients needing several mechanisms to control raised eye pressure.
full_description: Brinstar-BT combines brinzolamide, brimonidine and timolol for selected patients needing several mechanisms to control raised eye pressure. The ingredients reduce aqueous humour production, while brimonidine also supports outflow. It requires ophthalmologist-directed use, with attention to systemic beta-blocker effects, kidney function, sedation and the exact finished-product dosing instructions.
dosage_guidance:
Dosing and Schedule
Adults: instil 1 drop into each affected eye twice daily, approximately 12 hours apart. Continue regularly and review intraocular pressure at scheduled visits.

Administration Advice
Wash hands and place the prescribed drop inside the lower eyelid without touching the dropper tip. Close the eye gently. Separate other eye medicines by at least 5 minutes. Close the eyelids and press the inner corner for 1–2 minutes to reduce systemic absorption. Remove contact lenses as directed by the label. Shake if labelled as a suspension.

benefits.title: Open-Angle Glaucoma
benefits.description: Lowers raised eye pressure as part of prescribed treatment to reduce the risk of further optic nerve damage.

benefits.title: Ocular Hypertension
benefits.description: Helps control raised eye pressure when treatment is needed before detectable glaucomatous damage develops.

mechanisms.title: 01 — Inhibits Carbonic Anhydrase
mechanisms.description: Brinzolamide reduces bicarbonate-dependent aqueous humour secretion.

mechanisms.title: 02 — Adds Alpha-2 and Beta Receptor Effects
mechanisms.description: Brimonidine reduces secretion and promotes outflow, while timolol reduces beta-mediated aqueous production.

mechanisms.title: 03 — Provides Additive Pressure Control
mechanisms.description: The combined effects reduce intraocular fluid accumulation in appropriately selected patients.

safety_sections.title: Asthma and Heart Conditions
safety_sections.description: Timolol-containing drops are contraindicated in asthma, significant bradycardia, certain heart blocks and uncontrolled cardiac failure. Eye drops can have systemic effects.

safety_sections.title: Sulfonamide Reactions and Kidney Disease
safety_sections.description: Carbonic anhydrase inhibitors may cause sulfonamide-type hypersensitivity. Severe kidney impairment or acid-base disturbance requires avoidance or specialist review.

safety_sections.title: Infants, Children and Sedation
safety_sections.description: Brimonidine is contraindicated under 2 years and can cause serious sedation or breathing suppression in young children. Paediatric use requires specialist care.

safety_sections.title: Interactions and Monitoring
safety_sections.description: Review other glaucoma drops, cardiac medicines, sedatives and monoamine oxidase inhibitors. Monitor eye pressure, pulse and relevant systemic symptoms.

composition_summary: Methylcobalamin 2500 mcg Injection
short_description: Nervia contains methylcobalamin, an active form of vitamin B12 supplied for injection.
full_description: Nervia contains methylcobalamin, an active form of vitamin B12 supplied for injection. It is used when replacement is clinically indicated and an injectable route is selected. Vitamin B12 supports normal blood-cell formation and nerve function, with treatment tailored to the cause, severity and neurological features of deficiency.
dosage_guidance:
Dosing and Schedule
Your doctor or nurse will give you this medicine. Kindly do not self administer.

Administration Advice
A healthcare professional should administer by the route approved on the actual label. Do not self-inject or assume intravenous suitability from the ingredient name.

benefits.title: Vitamin B12 Deficiency
benefits.description: Replenishes vitamin B12 when deficiency is established and the selected formulation is appropriate to the cause and severity.

benefits.title: Deficiency-Associated Neurological or Blood Changes
benefits.description: Supports treatment of B12-related neuropathy or megaloblastic changes while the underlying cause and clinical response are monitored.

mechanisms.title: 01 — Provides Active Vitamin B12
mechanisms.description: Methylcobalamin supplies a coenzyme form of vitamin B12.

mechanisms.title: 02 — Supports Methylation Pathways
mechanisms.description: It participates in methionine synthase activity and linked folate metabolism.

mechanisms.title: 03 — Supports Blood and Nerve Function
mechanisms.description: Adequate B12 supports normal red blood cell formation and myelin-related nerve function when deficiency is corrected.

safety_sections.title: Diagnosis and Neurological Symptoms
safety_sections.description: Confirm the cause of deficiency. New weakness, gait disturbance or numbness needs prompt assessment rather than unsupervised supplementation.

safety_sections.title: Allergy and Monitoring
safety_sections.description: Avoid with relevant vitamin B12 or cobalt allergy. Monitor response and identify whether ongoing replacement is required.

safety_sections.title: Injection and Severe Anaemia
safety_sections.description: Observe for injection reactions. Severe megaloblastic anaemia may need early electrolyte and blood-count monitoring during effective replacement.

composition_summary: Methylcobalamin 500 mcg + Gabapentin 300 mg Tablets
short_description: Nervia-G combines gabapentin with methylcobalamin for prescribed management of neuropathic pain.
full_description: Nervia-G combines gabapentin with methylcobalamin for prescribed management of neuropathic pain. Gabapentin reduces abnormal excitatory nerve transmission, while methylcobalamin provides vitamin B12 support. The dose is introduced and adjusted according to symptoms, kidney function and tolerability, with gradual withdrawal when treatment is no longer required.
dosage_guidance:
Dosing and Schedule
Adults with normal kidney function: start with 1 tablet at bedtime on day 1, 1 tablet twice daily on day 2 and 1 tablet three times daily from day 3 if tolerated. This provides gabapentin 900 mg/day at the third step. Further titration requires review; reduce doses in kidney impairment.

Administration Advice
Swallow with water, with or without food. Space divided doses through the day and keep at least 2 hours after aluminium- or magnesium-containing antacids. Do not stop abruptly; taper under supervision.

benefits.title: Painful Diabetic Peripheral Neuropathy
benefits.description: May help reduce burning, tingling and shooting pain from an assessed diabetic peripheral neuropathy.

benefits.title: Postherpetic or Other Selected Nerve Pain
benefits.description: May be prescribed for persistent neuropathic pain after shingles or in other suitable conditions.

mechanisms.title: 01 — Binds Calcium-Channel Subunits
mechanisms.description: Gabapentin binds alpha-2-delta subunits of voltage-gated calcium channels.

mechanisms.title: 02 — Reduces Excitatory Neurotransmitter Release
mechanisms.description: Reduced transmitter release limits abnormal nerve-pain signalling.

mechanisms.title: 03 — Supports Vitamin B12-Dependent Function
mechanisms.description: Methylcobalamin supports normal nerve metabolism when vitamin B12 supply is insufficient.

safety_sections.title: Sleepiness, Dizziness and Driving
safety_sections.description: Avoid driving until the individual effect is known. Alcohol, opioids and other sedatives can increase sedation and breathing risk.

safety_sections.title: Kidney Function and Withdrawal
safety_sections.description: Gabapentinoids need renal dose review. Do not stop abruptly; follow the prescribed taper.

safety_sections.title: Mood Changes, Swelling and Allergy
safety_sections.description: Report new suicidal thoughts, marked mood changes, peripheral swelling or severe allergic symptoms promptly.

composition_summary: Methylcobalamin 1500 mcg Sublingual Tablet
short_description: Nervia OD contains methylcobalamin, an active vitamin B12 form, in a sublingual tablet.
full_description: Nervia OD contains methylcobalamin, an active vitamin B12 form, in a sublingual tablet. It supports replacement when vitamin B12 intake or status is inadequate and an oral approach is suitable. Appropriate correction supports normal nerve function and red blood cell formation, while the underlying cause of deficiency still needs assessment.
dosage_guidance:
Dosing and Schedule
Adults: take 1 sublingual tablet (1500 mcg) once daily. Review vitamin B12 status and neurological response to determine duration. Severe neurological deficiency or significant malabsorption requires assessment for injectable treatment.

Administration Advice
Place the tablet under the tongue and allow it to dissolve completely. Do not chew or swallow it immediately.

benefits.title: Vitamin B12 Deficiency
benefits.description: Replenishes vitamin B12 when deficiency is established and the selected formulation is appropriate to the cause and severity.

benefits.title: Deficiency-Associated Neurological or Blood Changes
benefits.description: Supports treatment of B12-related neuropathy or megaloblastic changes while the underlying cause and clinical response are monitored.

mechanisms.title: 01 — Provides Active Vitamin B12
mechanisms.description: Methylcobalamin supplies a coenzyme form of vitamin B12.

mechanisms.title: 02 — Supports Methylation Pathways
mechanisms.description: It participates in methionine synthase activity and linked folate metabolism.

mechanisms.title: 03 — Supports Blood and Nerve Function
mechanisms.description: Adequate B12 supports normal red blood cell formation and myelin-related nerve function when deficiency is corrected.

safety_sections.title: Diagnosis and Neurological Symptoms
safety_sections.description: Confirm the cause of deficiency. New weakness, gait disturbance or numbness needs prompt assessment rather than unsupervised supplementation.

safety_sections.title: Allergy and Monitoring
safety_sections.description: Avoid with relevant vitamin B12 or cobalt allergy. Monitor response and identify whether ongoing replacement is required.

safety_sections.title: Other Treatment Needs
safety_sections.description: Folate alone should not replace B12 when deficiency is present. Severe anaemia or malabsorption may need a different replacement plan.

composition_summary: Folic Acid (0.7 mg) + Methylcobalamin (1500 mcg) + Niacinamide (12 mg) & Vitamin-C (150)mg Injection
short_description: Nervia Forte combines methylcobalamin, folic acid, niacinamide and vitamin C in an injectable preparation for deficiency states.
full_description: Nervia Forte combines methylcobalamin, folic acid, niacinamide and vitamin C in an injectable preparation for deficiency states. The vitamins participate in blood formation, cellular metabolism and antioxidant functions. Injectable treatment should be used only when clinically indicated, with the route, ampoule volume and schedule confirmed from the finished product label.
dosage_guidance:
Dosing and Schedule
Your doctor or nurse will give you this medicine. Kindly do not self administer.

Administration Advice
Administration is by a trained healthcare professional using the route and dilution permitted by the actual label. Do not mix with other injections unless compatibility is established.

benefits.title: Selected Combined Vitamin Deficiencies
benefits.description: May be prescribed when assessment identifies a need for the supplied vitamins and an injectable formulation is appropriate.

benefits.title: Deficiency-Associated Blood or Neurological Changes
benefits.description: May support correction of relevant nutritional deficits alongside investigation and treatment of their cause.

mechanisms.title: 01 — Provides Active Vitamin B12
mechanisms.description: Methylcobalamin supplies a coenzyme form of vitamin B12.

mechanisms.title: 02 — Supports Cell and Energy Metabolism
mechanisms.description: Folate participates in DNA synthesis and niacinamide supports NAD-dependent cellular reactions.

mechanisms.title: 03 — Provides Additional Vitamin Support
mechanisms.description: Vitamin C contributes to antioxidant systems and collagen-related processes when nutritional supply is inadequate.

safety_sections.title: Injection Reactions and Allergy
safety_sections.description: Check ingredient and excipient allergy. Parenteral vitamins can cause serious hypersensitivity, requiring professional administration and observation.

safety_sections.title: Kidney Disease and Other Medicines
safety_sections.description: Review kidney disease, stone history and interacting treatments. Route, compatibility and repeated dosing require product-specific guidance.

composition_summary: Methylcobalamin 1500 mcg + alpha-lipoic acid 100 mcg as listed +  vitamin B 10 mg + vitamin B6 3mg + folic acid 1.5 mg per capsule
short_description: Nervia-Plus combines methylcobalamin and folic acid with alpha-lipoic acid and listed B-vitamin ingredients for prescribed nutritional support.
full_description: Nervia-Plus combines methylcobalamin and folic acid with alpha-lipoic acid and listed B-vitamin ingredients for prescribed nutritional support. These components participate in nerve-related and blood-forming pathways. The exact vitamin identities and alpha-lipoic acid unit need confirmation before a product-specific regimen or stronger clinical claims can be assigned.
dosage_guidance:
Dosing and Schedule
Take this medicine in the dose and duration as advised by your doctor. 

Administration Advice
Take with or immediately after a meal. Review continued use with the treating clinician and avoid overlapping supplements.

benefits.title: Selected B-Vitamin Insufficiency
benefits.description: May support replacement of relevant deficiencies after the complete formula and the patient’s requirements are confirmed.

benefits.title: Adjunct Nutritional Support in Neuropathy Care
benefits.description: May complement treatment when vitamin insufficiency contributes to symptoms. It is not a substitute for established neuropathic pain treatment.

mechanisms.title: 01 — Provides Active Vitamin B12
mechanisms.description: Methylcobalamin supplies a coenzyme form of vitamin B12.

mechanisms.title: 02 — Supports Folate-Dependent Processes
mechanisms.description: Folic acid contributes to normal DNA synthesis and blood-cell development after metabolic conversion.

mechanisms.title: 03 — Provides Additional Nutritional Components
mechanisms.description: The effects of the remaining ingredients depend on their verified identity and dose.

safety_sections.title: Unclear Ingredient Strengths
safety_sections.description: Do not assume the source’s alpha-lipoic acid 100 mcg means 100 mg or that unspecified vitamin B entries identify particular vitamins.

safety_sections.title: Neuropathy and Supplement Overlap
safety_sections.description: Investigate persistent neurological symptoms. Excess long-term vitamin B6 can itself cause neuropathy if that vitamin is included.

safety_sections.title: Glucose, Pregnancy and Organ Disease
safety_sections.description: Review glucose-lowering medicines, pregnancy, breastfeeding and kidney or liver disease before use.

composition_summary: Citicoline Sodium 500 mg + Piracetam 400 mg Tablets
short_description: Citirix-P combines citicoline with piracetam for neurological adjunctive use under specialist supervision.
full_description: Citirix-P combines citicoline with piracetam for neurological adjunctive use under specialist supervision. Citicoline participates in phospholipid pathways, while piracetam has effects on neuronal membrane-related function. The combination should be used only for an approved clinical indication, with discussion of evidence limitations and continued use of established stroke or rehabilitation care.
dosage_guidance:
Dosing and Schedule
Adults with suitable kidney function: take 1 tablet twice daily. Review neurological response and kidney function before continuing or increasing treatment.

Administration Advice
Swallow with water after breakfast and the evening meal. Do not stop established neurological treatment or substitute this combination for rehabilitation.

benefits.title: Adjunctive Management after Ischaemic Stroke
benefits.description: May be prescribed where the exact combination has a local approved indication. It does not replace reperfusion, antithrombotic treatment or rehabilitation.

benefits.title: Selected Post-Stroke Functional or Cognitive Symptoms
benefits.description: Any continued use for residual symptoms requires specialist review and label confirmation. A reliable recovery benefit is not established for this exact blend.

mechanisms.title: 01 — Provides Phospholipid Precursors
mechanisms.description: Citicoline is metabolised to compounds used in phosphatidylcholine synthesis.

mechanisms.title: 02 — Provides Piracetam-Related Activity
mechanisms.description: Piracetam influences neuronal membrane-related processes, although its full mechanism is not established.

mechanisms.title: 03 — Provides a Proposed Supportive Action
mechanisms.description: Biochemical plausibility does not establish improved neurological recovery. Clinical benefit is uncertain and treatment remains adjunctive.

safety_sections.title: Evidence and Urgent Stroke Care
safety_sections.description: Do not delay emergency stroke treatment, rehabilitation or established secondary prevention. Large trials did not show routine functional benefit from citicoline in stroke or brain injury.

safety_sections.title: Kidney Function and Bleeding
safety_sections.description: Piracetam is renally cleared and may affect platelet function. Review kidney impairment, anticoagulants, bleeding disorders and planned surgery.

safety_sections.title: Diagnosis and Special Populations
safety_sections.description: Confirm the approved indication and avoid use in relevant contraindicated conditions, including cerebral haemorrhage. Pregnancy and breastfeeding require specialist advice.

composition_summary: Methylcobalamin 1500 mcg + Pregabalin 75 mg (SR) Tablet
short_description: Nervia-PG combines pregabalin with methylcobalamin for prescribed management of neuropathic pain.
full_description: Nervia-PG combines pregabalin with methylcobalamin for prescribed management of neuropathic pain. Pregabalin reduces abnormal excitatory nerve transmission, while methylcobalamin provides vitamin B12 support. The dose is introduced and adjusted according to symptoms, kidney function and tolerability, with gradual withdrawal when treatment is no longer required.
dosage_guidance:
Dosing and Schedule
Take this medicine in the dose and duration as advised by your doctor. 

Administration Advice
Swallow the sustained-release tablet whole with water. Do not crush or chew. Adjust pregabalin dosing for kidney function and taper over at least 1 week when discontinuing.

benefits.title: Painful Diabetic Peripheral Neuropathy
benefits.description: May help reduce burning, tingling and shooting pain from an assessed diabetic peripheral neuropathy.

benefits.title: Postherpetic or Other Selected Nerve Pain
benefits.description: May be prescribed for persistent neuropathic pain after shingles or in other suitable conditions.

mechanisms.title: 01 — Binds Calcium-Channel Subunits
mechanisms.description: Pregabalin binds alpha-2-delta subunits of voltage-gated calcium channels.

mechanisms.title: 02 — Reduces Excitatory Neurotransmitter Release
mechanisms.description: Reduced transmitter release limits abnormal nerve-pain signalling.

mechanisms.title: 03 — Supports Vitamin B12-Dependent Function
mechanisms.description: Methylcobalamin supports normal nerve metabolism when vitamin B12 supply is insufficient.

safety_sections.title: Sleepiness, Dizziness and Driving
safety_sections.description: Avoid driving until the individual effect is known. Alcohol, opioids and other sedatives can increase sedation and breathing risk.

safety_sections.title: Kidney Function and Withdrawal
safety_sections.description: Gabapentinoids need renal dose review. Do not stop abruptly; follow the prescribed taper.

safety_sections.title: Mood Changes, Swelling and Allergy
safety_sections.description: Report new suicidal thoughts, marked mood changes, peripheral swelling or severe allergic symptoms promptly.

composition_summary: Propranolol 40 mg SR Tablets
short_description: Pulsorex contains sustained-release propranolol, a non-selective beta-blocker used in selected cardiovascular and neurological conditions.
full_description: Pulsorex contains sustained-release propranolol, a non-selective beta-blocker used in selected cardiovascular and neurological conditions. It reduces beta-adrenergic responses, helping control heart rate or symptoms such as tremor. The dose is individualised and monitored, particularly in people with low blood pressure, diabetes, breathing problems or other cardiac medicines.
dosage_guidance:
Dosing and Schedule
Adults starting this 40 mg sustained-release formulation: take 1 tablet once daily. Review pulse, blood pressure and indication-specific response before titration. Migraine prevention and essential tremor can require a higher maintenance dose; do not increase independently.

Administration Advice
Swallow whole with water at the same time each morning, consistently in relation to food. Do not crush or chew. Continue regularly and taper gradually when stopping.

benefits.title: Migraine Prevention
benefits.description: May reduce migraine frequency when used regularly. It does not treat an acute migraine attack.

benefits.title: Essential Tremor
benefits.description: May reduce tremor severity in suitable patients after the cause has been assessed.

benefits.title: Selected Heart-Rate or Blood-Pressure Disorders
benefits.description: May be prescribed for appropriate cardiovascular indications with pulse and blood-pressure monitoring.

mechanisms.title: 01 — Blocks Beta-Adrenergic Receptors
mechanisms.description: Propranolol blocks beta-1 and beta-2 receptors.

mechanisms.title: 02 — Reduces Sympathetic Responses
mechanisms.description: It lowers heart rate and contractility and reduces beta-mediated tremor.

mechanisms.title: 03 — Supports the Prescribed Indication
mechanisms.description: Sustained beta-blockade can help prevent migraine or control selected tremor and cardiovascular symptoms.

safety_sections.title: Asthma and Cardiac Contraindications
safety_sections.description: Avoid with asthma, significant bradycardia, relevant heart block or uncontrolled heart failure. Seek help for wheeze or fainting.

safety_sections.title: Diabetes and Interactions
safety_sections.description: May mask hypoglycaemia warning signs. Review verapamil, diltiazem, other beta-blockers and medicines affecting blood pressure or rhythm.

safety_sections.title: Abrupt Withdrawal
safety_sections.description: Sudden stopping may worsen angina or trigger cardiovascular events. Follow a gradual prescriber-directed reduction.

composition_summary: Citicoline 500 mg per tablet
short_description: Citirix contains citicoline, a precursor involved in cell-membrane phospholipid pathways, used as an adjunct in selected neurological care settings.
full_description: Citirix contains citicoline, a precursor involved in cell-membrane phospholipid pathways, used as an adjunct in selected neurological care settings. Proposed effects relate to membrane and neurotransmitter metabolism. Evidence for improved recovery after stroke or brain injury is inconsistent, so use should complement established treatment and specialist-directed rehabilitation.
dosage_guidance:
Dosing and Schedule
Adults: take 1 tablet (500 mg) twice daily when citicoline is prescribed as adjunctive therapy. Review clinical benefit before continuing long term.

Administration Advice
Swallow with water in the morning and evening, with or without food. Continue the prescribed rehabilitation and other neurological treatment.

benefits.title: Selected Post-Stroke Adjunctive Care
benefits.description: May be prescribed where locally approved as an adjunct. It is not a substitute for acute stroke treatment or secondary prevention.

benefits.title: Selected Neurological Rehabilitation Settings
benefits.description: Any use after brain injury or for cognitive symptoms should follow the approved label and specialist review, with discussion of uncertain benefit.

mechanisms.title: 01 — Provides Phospholipid Precursors
mechanisms.description: Citicoline is metabolised to compounds used in phosphatidylcholine synthesis.

mechanisms.title: 02 — Supports Membrane-Related Biochemistry
mechanisms.description: These substrates participate in normal cell membrane and neurotransmitter pathways.

mechanisms.title: 03 — Provides a Proposed Supportive Action
mechanisms.description: Biochemical plausibility does not establish improved neurological recovery. Clinical benefit is uncertain and treatment remains adjunctive.

safety_sections.title: Evidence and Urgent Stroke Care
safety_sections.description: Do not delay emergency stroke treatment, rehabilitation or established secondary prevention. Large trials did not show routine functional benefit from citicoline in stroke or brain injury.

safety_sections.title: Individual Assessment and Tolerance
safety_sections.description: Headache, gastrointestinal symptoms or blood-pressure changes may occur. Review the neurological diagnosis and ongoing need with the specialist.

safety_sections.title: Pregnancy and Other Medicines
safety_sections.description: Pregnancy, breastfeeding and interacting medicines, including levodopa, require individual review.

composition_summary: Citicoline 250ml/mg injection
short_description: Citirix 250 contains citicoline, a precursor involved in cell-membrane phospholipid pathways, used as an adjunct in selected neurological care settings.
full_description: Citirix 250 contains citicoline, a precursor involved in cell-membrane phospholipid pathways, used as an adjunct in selected neurological care settings. Proposed effects relate to membrane and neurotransmitter metabolism.
dosage_guidance:
Dosing and Schedule
Your doctor or nurse will give you this medicine. Kindly do not self administer.

Administration Advice
A healthcare professional should administer by the actual approved route using verified concentration and dilution instructions. Do not self-inject.

benefits.title: Selected Post-Stroke Adjunctive Care

benefits.title: Selected Neurological Rehabilitation Settings

mechanisms.title: 02 — Supports Membrane-Related Biochemistry
mechanisms.description: These substrates participate in normal cell membrane and neurotransmitter pathways.

mechanisms.title: 03 — Provides a Proposed Supportive Action

safety_sections.title: Individual Assessment and Tolerance
